chunks: Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from Dawud and Ali, his two brothers, from Hammad from Hariz from Burayd, who said:
I saw him perform ghusl on the night of the 23rd twice: once at the beginning of the night and once at the end of the night.

key_terms.لَيْلَةِ ثَلَاثٍ وَعِشْرِينَ: the night of the 23rd (referring to Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: How many times should one perform ghusl on the 23rd night of Ramadan according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the specific practice of performing ghusl twice on Laylat al-Qadr (the 23rd night), once at the beginning and once at the end of the night, to ensure ritual purity for extended night worship. This dual performance underscores the Shia emphasis on maximizing spiritual preparation and devotion during the most auspicious nights of Ramadan, distinguishing it from the single ghusl often cited in other traditions.
